description.narrative: (Ethiopia): Ethiopia is a youthful population with more than 70 percent of its population under the age of 30. The demographic challenges are enormous but also can create opportunities. Ethiopian youth are faced with large under-employment and unemployment and have fewer opportunities to grow to their full potential due to the prolonged conflict in the north, drought in the lowlands, economic hardships, and high inflation. These factors in turn create perfect conditions for groups seeking to mobilize youth for violence. ..The Integrated Youth Activity (Kefeta) is a youth-led activity that empowers 15 to 29 year-old youth to advance their own social, economic, and civic development so they productively contribute to the development of their communities and Ethiopia's peace and stability. Kefeta will implement holistic and integrated youth programming directed at secondary cities affected by conflict and drought while preventing violence in other urban areas and maintain much needed stability through engaging youth in peacebuilding and stabilization efforts...Kefeta will build youth resilience, prevent gender-based violence against young women and girls, and provide essential youth-friendly health and financial services. Funds will strengthen youth networks and establish new youth coalitions and youth groups in educational institutions, community settings, and large workplaces to promote sustained dialogue among youth groups. Kefeta also engages the private sector and builds the capacity of youth-serving organizations for sustainable impact beyond the life of the activity. .Kefeta will contribute to USAID youth in development policy goals, supporting U.S. Foreign Policy objectives through engaging youth in promoting peace and stability in times of rapid change, conflict, or crises......
